name: Ala-Archa National Park
elev: From ~1500 m in the lower part of the gorge to 4895 m (Semenov-Tyan-Shansky Peak) — asiamixtravel 2026. Route landmarks: Ak-Sai waterfall ~2860 m, Ratsek hut ~3380 m (adventuresoflilnicki, 16.09.2026); the starting zone at the alpine camp is about 2150 m (calculated: waterfall 2860 m minus a 700 m ascent per hiking.kg).
short: Ala-Archa is a state nature park in a gorge of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too ~40 km south of Bishkek: spruce and juniper (archa) forests, glaciers and peaks up to 4895 m, and the country's most popular day treks.
desc: Ala-Archa is a mountain nature park in Alamudun district of Chuy region, in the gorge of the Ala-Archa River on the northern slope of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too. Elevations range from ~1500 m to 4895 m; in the upper reaches are the Ak-Sai, Adygene and other glaciers, and on the slopes Schrenk spruce and the archa (juniper) that gave the gorge its name. Since 1 May 2025, by presidential order, cars with internal combustion engines have been banned from the park: guests leave their cars at the parking lot by the checkpoint (≈700 spaces), and from there ~80 electric buses carry them free of charge (about 12 km to the alpine camp and the start of the trails). On site are a restaurant, a cafe, cottages, a yurt village and gas grills (campfires and wood-fired barbecues are banned). The classic routes are the Ak-Sai waterfall (4.3 km, +700 m), the Ratsek hut (~3380 m) by the Ak-Sai glacier, and the Adygene gorge; in winter a ski base operates nearby.
guide: Ala-Archa is the best way to get into real high mountains in a single day from Bishkek: take bus No. 1 from Usubaliev Square and in an hour you're at the checkpoint. From there a free electric bus takes you to the alpine camp, where all the trails start. For a first visit the Ak-Sai waterfall is enough: 4.3 km and +700 m, about 2.5 hours up, with a view of the glacial cirque. If you're well acclimatized, continue to the Ratsek hut (~3380 m), but set out early: in the afternoon the weather in the mountains often turns bad. Campfires are banned, so bring a thermos and a snack or eat at the cafe by the alpine camp.
see: Walking sections along the Ala-Archa, the alpine camp, the Ak-Sai waterfall; the Ratsek hut is a separate, harder hike.
skip: You've already hiked similar gorges (Alamedin, Kegety) and are looking for solitude — it's crowded here on weekends. You want to drive your own car to the trails — since May 2025 only electric cars are allowed inside. You aren't ready for a 700+ m climb even for the “easy” waterfall.
diff: The park has no single difficulty level: a walk along the river, the trail to the waterfall and the climb to the Ratsek hut require different levels of preparation.
when: May to October is the main hiking season (asiamixtravel 2026); July to September is the best time for the Ratsek hut. In winter the park is open (electric buses run around the clock per hiking.kg), the trails are under snow and avalanche-prone, and there is skiing nearby.
hours: The park is open daily; electric buses run around the clock (hiking.kg), and Google and 2GIS give “24 hours”. The administration office is open 09:00–17:30, closed Sat–Sun (park website) — don't confuse this with the checkpoint's hours. Bus No. 1 runs 08:00–19:00. Checkpoint: +996 312 883 205.
daytime: Early morning: fewer people on the electric buses and on the trail, stable weather; in the mountains after noon there are more often clouds and thunderstorms. On weekends arrive at opening — there are queues for the electric bus (editorial).
how: Bus No. 1 (semi-express): old Usubaliev Square (corner of Abdymomunov and Erkindik) → park checkpoint, 08:00–19:00, every 20–30 min, 45–60 min on the way, 50 som cash / 40 som by card (economist.kg 05.2025; adventuresoflilnicki 09.2026; the route through the city was changed 02.09.2025). Taxi 40–60 min. Cars with internal combustion engines are left in the parking lot at the checkpoint, and from there a free electric bus runs ~12 km to the alpine camp.
needcar: To get there — yes, but the city bus No. 1 or a taxi is enough. Inside the park a private vehicle isn't needed: free electric buses run to the alpine camp and the start of the trails.
self: Yes: bus No. 1, a ticket at the checkpoint (by QR code), the free electric bus and the marked popular trails. For the Ratsek hut and the glaciers you need mountain experience; overnight stays in the hut are booked through Ak-Sai Travel.
roadtype: Paved road from Bishkek to the checkpoint (a mountain serpentine at the end); inside the park, a paved road for electric buses to the alpine camp; above that, mountain trails.
traveltime: From central Bishkek: bus No. 1 — 45–60 min, taxi — 40–60 min (~40 km; hiking.kg — 43 km, 1 h 10 min). From the alpine camp: Ak-Sai waterfall — 4.3 km, ~2.5 h up, +700 m (hiking.kg); Ratsek hut — 5.7 km one way (asiamixtravel), usually 3.5–4.5 h up (editorial).
stay: In the park: a hotel/cottages at the alpine camp, a yurt village, a restaurant (banks.kg 2025); the Ratsek hut (~3380 m, book via Ak-Sai Travel); nearby — ALTO Cabins, Manzara A-Frames, the Kashka-Suu ski base (adventuresoflilnicki 2026). 2026 prices are not given in the sources.
net: A mobile signal is usually available at the checkpoint and the alpine camp, but unstable higher up the trails; “don't count on reliable coverage in the mountains” (asiamixtravel 2026). The operator by section is not confirmed.
entry: Since 11.06.2026: adults 250 som, children 7–14 years 180 som, under 7 free; entry of a private electric car 880 som (24.kg 11.06.2026; asiamixtravel 2026; Reporter.kg). Before that (from 01.05.2025): 200/150 som, electric car 800 som (banks.kg, economist.kg). Ticket by QR code at the checkpoint. Parking at the checkpoint — 50 som (hiking.kg, undated). The tariff on the park's website (free on foot, cars 700 som) is outdated.
transfer: Bus No. 1 — 50 som cash / 40 som by card (2025–2026); taxi Bishkek — Ala-Archa 800–1500 som one way (vc.ru 2026); tours $30–80 per person; the electric bus inside the park — free.
bring: Trekking shoes, a windbreaker and a warm layer (elevations 2150–3400 m), 1.5–2 L of water and a snack (campfires are banned), sun protection, cash for the checkpoint (card terminals are unreliable — vc.ru), poles for the descent; for Ratsek — a headlamp and a down jacket.
warn: Since 1 May 2025 cars with internal combustion engines are banned — parking at the checkpoint and the electric bus. Campfires and wood-fired barbecues are banned (only gas grills in designated zones). Above the alpine camp the elevation is 2800–3400 m: altitude sickness, sudden changes of weather, avalanches and rockfalls out of season; turn back if visibility worsens (asiamixtravel). Tariffs change — check at the checkpoint +996 312 883 205.
food: A restaurant and a cafe with drinks and pastries at the alpine camp, a yurt village (banks.kg, 2025); mountain tea from a thermos and a picnic at the gas grills in designated zones are popular. Specific menus and prices are not confirmed.
reviews: Google Maps: 4.7/5, 3871 ratings (as of 03.10.2026). Yandex Maps and TripAdvisor (page d735790) have many reviews, the rating could not be captured in this environment; Tripster excursions to Ala-Archa have their own reviews. Pros: closeness to Bishkek, views, the electric buses and the cleanliness after the 2025 reform; cons: queues and crowds on weekends, rising entry prices, the ban on private cars.
p.sum: Easiest is bus No. 1 from the old Usubaliev Square (50 som cash / 40 by card, 08:00–19:00, every 20–30 min) or a taxi ≈1000 som to the checkpoint; cars with internal combustion engines are left in the large lot at the entrance. At the checkpoint a ticket is 250 som (children 7–14 — 180), then a free electric bus ~12 km to the alpine camp (every 10–15 min in the daytime). Since 19.02.2026 a Doppelmayr gondola has operated at the alpine camp (1 km, 2166→2494 m, 600 som round trip, cashless only, closed on Tuesdays). The classic day hike is the Ak-Sai waterfall (≈4 km, +450–700 m); for the prepared, the Ratsek hut (6.4 km, +1100 m, 3380 m; bunk 700–1400 som, book via Ak-Sai Travel). Set out early: on weekends there are queues for the electric bus.

p.iti.0.title: 1 day — Ak-Sai waterfall
p.iti.0.plan: 07:30 bus No. 1 from Usubaliev Sq. → 08:30 checkpoint, ticket 250 som → electric bus → 09:00 start → 11:00 Ak-Sai waterfall → 12:30 “Broken Heart”, descend by gondola if you like → 14:00 lunch in a cafe → a walk along the river → 17:00 electric bus and bus to Bishkek (the last ~19:00).
p.iti.1.title: 2 days — Ratsek hut
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: an early start, by 09:00 set out from the alpine camp, past the waterfall to the hut (4–5 h), night at Ratsek (book via Ak-Sai). Day 2: sunrise on the Ak-Sai glacier moraine, descend by lunch (2.5 h), electric bus, Bishkek.
p.iti.2.title: Combination
p.iti.2.plan: Ala-Archa in the morning → Koy-Tash (hot springs) → Kara-Bulak or Chunkurchak in the evening; neighboring: Kara-Bulak (11.7 km as the crow flies), Chunkurchak.
p.season: May to October is the main season; July to September is the best time for Ratsek and Adygene; weekends — queues for the electric bus. November to April: the park is open, the trails are under snow, avalanche-prone above the alpine camp; ice climbing and skiing (Kashka-Suu). On holidays entry is sometimes free (1 May 2025). New tariffs since 08.06.2026.
p.budget.economy: ≈1000–1600 som/person: bus 2×50, entry 250, snack/cafe 500–600, gondola 600 (optional); with an overnight at Ratsek +700–1400 and food 900–1300.
p.budget.comfort: ≈5000–15,000 som/person: taxi 2×1000, tour $30–80, gondola 600, a room at the alpine camp 4000–9000 or an A-frame from 11,000 som.
p.permits: Ticket at the checkpoint (QR): adults 250 som, children 7–14 — 180, under 7 free (since 08.06.2026); electric car 880 som. The electric bus is included. The gondola is extra, cashless only. No border permit needed. Campfires are banned.
p.access: With children — yes (electric bus, a 1.3 km path along the river, the gondola; child ticket 180 som). Older people — electric bus + gondola + the path along the river. Stroller — the path along the river is suitable (eurasia.travel), the rest is not. The 2026 tariff has no discounts for people with disabilities (criticized on social media). Dogs — no rules found.
